title: OBSERVATION OF ANESTHETIC CONSUMPTION IN CANNABINOID USERS TO IMPROVE ANESTHETIC MANAGEMENT AND POSTOPERATIVE OPIATE USE
summary:
Adult patients who voluntarily undergo planned surgery in the fields of orthopaedics, trauma surgery, general surgery, urology, maxillofacial surgery or thoracic surgery are always asked whether they use recreational substances such as cannabis, opiates or other such substances. If a patient states that they use these substances, they are offered participation in this observational study. However, patients who do not consume such substances can also participate if they match the age, gender, state of health and planned operation with users already included in the study. These non-users then form the comparison group.
If a patient has been informed in detail about the study and agrees, general personal and specific medical data is recorded. On the day of the operation, the patient is asked to provide a urine sample either on the ward or in the operating room. The anesthesia is then induced as is usual in the respective hospital. All medication administered during anesthesia, important bodily functions and the consumption of anesthetic gases are recorded in detail. During anesthesia, a device that monitors the depth of anesthesia (BIS monitoring) is used as standard.
After the operation, the current pain intensity and the consumption of painkillers are recorded in the recovery room until the patient returns to the normal ward. This is checked again the next day.
There is a follow-up appointment about 30 days after the operation, either in person or by telephone. The patient's consumption of opiates and other painkillers since discharge (whether yes/no, which drugs, what dosage and how long they were taken), new pain disorders and whether the patient is still alive are recorded. After this date, the study is completed for the individual patient.
For better comparability, selected control patients are included who are taking part in the same examinations but who have not been shown to consume cannabis.

interventions.name: Patients who use cannabinoids or opiods and get an elective operation
Cannabinoid and opiate-naive patients undergoing elective surgery

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients undergoing elective
surgery in the fields of a) orthopaedics, b)
trauma surgery, c) general surgery, d) urology, e)
maxillofacial surgery or f) thoracic surgery
operations
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Patients who receive epidural or spinal anesthesia
2.	Patients with a chronic pain diagnosis
3.	Patients who had anesthesia in the last four weeks before the current operation
4.	Patients who require ICU treatment
5.	Patients requiring mechanical ventilation after leaving the operation room
6.	Patients who receive clonidine as medication as part of a disease 
7.	Patients who receive pregabalin or gabapentin or related active substances as medication in the context of a disease 
8.	Persons with any kind of dependency on the investigator or employed by the sponsor or investigator.
9.	Pregnancy or breastfeeding
